summary: The Global Youth Summit for Climate Action, held from September 17, 2023 in Geneva, Switzerland, gathered over 5,000 young leaders, innovators and activists over four days. It focuses on measurable solutions, start-ups, education, networking and media training, while demanding stronger climate policy including a legally binding international treaty. Featured figures include Makena Njeri, Lars Olsen and Isabella Zhang, along with start-ups such as GreenSpirits and EcoThread.
one_line: Over 5,000 young climate activists and innovators met in Geneva in September 2023 to demand action and launch start-ups and projects.
key_facts: The Global Youth Summit for Climate Action was held on September 17, 2023 in Geneva, Switzerland.
Over 5,000 young leaders, innovators, and activists attended the summit, which runs four days.
Kenyan activist Makena Njeri, 23, and Norwegian innovator Lars Olsen, 19, are among the figures spearheading the event.
Makena Njeri gave the keynote address, saying: "We are not the leaders of tomorrow; we are the leaders of today."
Isabella Zhang, a 16-year-old climate poet, emerged as a notable voice at the summit.
The "Tech for Green" session showcased prototypes of renewable energy solutions, waste reduction technologies, and sustainable urban planning models.
Lars Olsen presented a robotic system designed to clean ocean plastics.
GreenSpirits is a start-up planning to use drone technology to reduce water usage and pesticide application in agriculture.
EcoThread, founded by Suhani Patel from India, is a sustainable clothing line using recycled materials.
Attendees are pushing for an international legally binding treaty with aggressive targets and transparent tracking.
The shared project "United Roots for a Greener Future" plans to crowdsource and plant millions of trees worldwide.
Juanita Alvarez from Bolivia and Tendai Mutambu from Zimbabwe partnered to help rural communities switch to solar energy.
The summit offers "Youth Teach-In" sessions, scholarships and research grants, and media training workshops.
Diego Sanchez from Chile and Fatoumata Diawara from Senegal emerged as spokespersons from the media training.
